comments.content: The configured value is discarded: the dict is hardcoded to `-1` even though this branch is guarded by `self.thinking_budget is not None`. `self.thinking_budget` is never read anywhere else in the file, so user-supplied budgets (including `0` to disable thinking) are silently overridden with dynamic thinking, which affects cost/latency and makes the field meaningless.

comments.content: Changing the default from `None` to `0` makes `if self.thinking_budget is not None:` always true, so `thinking_config` is now sent on every request. `VerifiedGeminiModels` includes models that do not support thinking (`gemma-3-*`, `gemini-2.0-flash-exp`, `gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05`), which typically causes the API to reject the request with 400. It also unconditionally overwrites a `thinking_config` the caller passed via `config`. Consider keeping `None` as the default, or gating the assignment on model capability / on an explicit user opt-in.

comments.content: The manual retry loop (10 attempts with exponential backoff) was removed on the assumption that the SDK retries internally, but the comment is inaccurate: `_get_client_params` only forwards `http_options` (which is `None` by default) and never configures `HttpRetryOptions`. Unlike the other providers (`openai`/`anthropic`/`groq`/`openrouter` set `max_retries` on the client), Google now has no retry path at all, so transient 429/503/timeouts surface immediately. Either configure retry options on the client or keep an explicit retry loop.

comments.content: `asyncio.CancelledError` derives from `BaseException`, not `Exception`, so it can never be the object bound inside `except Exception as e` — `isinstance(e, asyncio.CancelledError)` is always `False`. The enhanced 504 timeout diagnosis branch is therefore dead code (only the `str(type(e))` fallback can ever match), and real cancellations bypass this handler entirely. Catch `asyncio.CancelledError` in a separate `except` clause if that diagnosis is intended.
